stepNotes.1: Single 74-line module, 16 exports, consumed by 12 route files under src/server/routes — a shared request-param dependency, not a leaf.
stepNotes.2: First trust boundary after the network read: branded-id casting via SessionID.make (branded.ts:19-21) is unchecked, so all validation burden sits on the upstream validator() mount.
stepNotes.3: parseSessionID is correct only if SESSION_ID_PARAM is registered upstream; withRouteParam reads params[key] with no fallback so a missing key yields undefined typed as TValue. No active key-mismatch in consumers read.
stepNotes.4: No hot-path issue: closures + one record lookup; zod schemas are module-level constants; parseExistingSessionID is a single indexed Session.get read.
stepNotes.5: withRouteParam/with* family earns its keep (12 consumers) but is typed c:any, diverging from the SessionRouteContext used by the parse* helpers; PROVIDER_ID_PARAM is the only schema with OpenAPI .meta description.
stepNotes.6: parseExistingSessionID (route-params.ts:38) is dead — zero callers repo-wide and policed away by session-messages.test.ts:379; it also bypasses the 409 cross-project guard that its replacement parseCurrentProjectSessionID enforces.
stepNotes.7: No direct unit test; coverage is structural (session-messages.test.ts:362-400 greps session-impl.ts source to force parseCurrentProjectSessionID and forbid parseExistingSessionID/parseSessionID on destructive+detail routes). withRouteParam generic path and withProviderID/withPtyID/withProjectID adapters have no behavioral test.
stepNotes.8: Four findings recorded: MEDIUM dead guard-bypassing export (parseExistingSessionID), LOW implicit-validation precondition, LOW inconsistent OpenAPI descriptions, INFO parallel context contracts. No Critical.
stepNotes.9: No Critical findings -> no reverify.md second pass required; gate before sign-off is typecheck + session-messages.test.ts after removing parseExistingSessionID; finding 1 is the only one worth acting on this wave.
